title: Fatigue and Palpitations, Internal Medicine
objectives: Document two related complaints without conflating them
Correctly convert lay descriptions of palpitations and fatigue to clinical terminology
Avoid fabricating a value for any vital sign or lab that was not provided

encounter.chiefComplaintRaw: feeling tired and heart racing on and off for 2 weeks
encounter.narrative: Patient reports feeling unusually tired for the past two weeks, along with intermittent episodes where his heart feels like it's racing, lasting a few minutes at a time. Denies chest pain. Denies fainting or near-fainting. No fever. Reports drinking more coffee than usual recently. No known thyroid problems. Denies shortness of breath at rest, but notes mild breathlessness climbing stairs, which is new for him.
encounter.hpi: Onset 2 weeks ago, intermittent episodes of palpitations lasting minutes, associated fatigue, increased caffeine intake, new mild exertional dyspnea.
encounter.ros: Denies chest pain, denies syncope, denies fever, positive for exertional dyspnea, positive for palpitations, positive for fatigue.
encounter.history: No known cardiac or thyroid history.
encounter.physicalExam: Alert, no acute distress. No exam findings described in this encounter beyond patient-reported symptoms.
encounter.assessment: Palpitations and fatigue, etiology undetermined; new mild exertional dyspnea. Differential includes arrhythmia, anemia, thyroid dysfunction, and excess caffeine intake.
encounter.plan: Obtain ECG and basic labs; advise reducing caffeine intake; return precautions for chest pain, syncope, or worsening dyspnea.

requiredDocumentation.description: Document both presenting complaints without conflating them into one
requiredDocumentation.sourceFact: feeling tired and heart racing on and off for 2 weeks
acceptableVariants: fatigue and intermittent palpitations x2 weeks

requiredDocumentation.description: Document absence of fainting/near-fainting using clinical terminology
Document the new exertional shortness of breath using clinical terminology
requiredDocumentation.sourceFact: mild breathlessness climbing stairs, which is new for him

requiredDocumentation.description: Document the increased caffeine intake as a relevant contributing factor
requiredDocumentation.sourceFact: drinking more coffee than usual recently

optionalDocumentation.description: Document absence of known thyroid problems

commonErrors.description: Learner documents a specific heart rate (e.g. 'HR 110') though no vital signs were given in the encounter
Learner merges fatigue and palpitations into a single vague complaint, losing clinically relevant detail
Learner omits the new exertional dyspnea, which is clinically relevant to the differential
Learner writes 'heart racing' verbatim instead of converting to clinical terminology
